page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The configuration includes 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA. For memory and storage, the server is provisioned with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, alongside 800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is included in this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is positioned in the top tier with a score of 3201.49, whereas multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category at 50410.87. Memory performance is a notable strength, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25% at 2907.91, although raw memory bandwidth tests for large blocks remain in the average tier. In database and transactional workloads, the instance achieves average ratings, processing 31.17 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 7721.28 on PassMark database operations. Large language model inference using a small 135M model demonstrates strong text generation speeds at 293.29 tokens per second, while prompt processing and medium 7B model inference perform at average levels.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a qualitative balance between dedicated compute cores and high memory capacity. The high memory-to-core ratio makes it a cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive multi-core scaling. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage eliminates the need for external storage attachments for primary operations. This server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, caching layers such as Redis, medium-scale web serving, and lightweight LLM text generation tasks.
